error.IndentationError.body: The spaces at the start of your lines (indentation) don't line up, starting from line {line}. Python uses indentation to tell which lines belong under an if or for. Check that the lines right below a line ending in a colon (:) are all indented by the same amount.
error.IndentationError.detective: The spaces at the start of a line look suspicious. The trail starts from line {line}. Python reads indentation to tell which lines belong to an if or for gang. Line up the lines under each colon (:) and compare: are they all indented the same?
error.IndentationError.title: Indentation mismatch ({type})
error.InputMissing.body: input() tried to read a value, but there was no input left (from line {line}). This happens when you call input() more times than the question gives inputs. Count the inputs the question gives, then count your input() calls.
error.InputMissing.detective: The witness has stopped talking. An input() is still waiting for an answer, and the trail starts from line {line}. Did you call input() more times than there are inputs? Compare the question's input count with your input() calls.
error.InputMissing.title: More input needed
error.NameError.body: Python doesn't recognize a name, coming from line {line}. Usually it's text that's missing its quotes: print(hello) makes Python look for a variable called hello. It can also be a typo or a variable used before it's created. If it's text, add quotes. If it's a variable, check the spelling and make sure it's set before you use it.
error.NameError.detective: A name with no ID has appeared! The case starts from line {line}. A string that lost its quotes (like print(hello)) may be posing as a name. Or a letter in the spelling changed, or a variable was called before it was created. Check that name's quotes, its spelling, and the line where it first shows up, one by one.
error.NameError.title: Unknown name ({type})
error.OutputLimit.body: Your code printed so much that it was stopped partway. The output came from line {line}. This happens when a print() inside a loop runs forever, or a huge number of times. Check how many times the loop runs and that it has a proper stopping condition.
error.OutputLimit.detective: Paper is piling up like a mountain! There was so much output that the investigation stopped. The case started with output from line {line}. Did a loop run far more times than expected, maybe forever? Track the loop count and its stopping condition.
error.OutputLimit.title: Too much output
error.SyntaxError.body: Python found something that breaks its grammar rules, coming from line {line}[[ (sometimes the real slip is on the line just before)]]. Usually a quote or bracket was opened but never closed, or the colon (:) at the end of an if or for line is missing. Check that every opening quote and bracket has a matching closing one.
error.SyntaxError.detective: Hmm, I see traces of broken grammar. The trail starts from line {line}[[ (the line just before it looks suspicious too)]]. The suspects: a quote that lost its partner, an unclosed bracket, a missing colon (:). Grab your magnifying glass and match each opening symbol with its closing one.
error.SyntaxError.title: Broken syntax ({type})
error.Timeout.body: Your code didn't finish within {seconds} seconds, so it was stopped. This time there's no line number to go on. Usually a loop never reaches its stopping condition and keeps going. Check that the value in your while condition changes every time the loop runs.
error.Timeout.detective: I see footprints going round and round the same spot. The code didn't finish within {seconds} seconds. The likely culprit: a loop that never reaches its stopping condition. Track whether the value in the condition really changes on every loop.
error.Timeout.title: Time's up
error.TypeError.body: You're mixing types that don't go together (from line {line}). This usually happens when you join a string and a number with +. Try matching the types: use int() to do math, or str() to join them as text.
error.TypeError.detective: Two values that don't belong together were caught side by side. The trail starts from line {line}. Mixing a string and a number as-is is the prime suspect. Check each value's ID (string or number?) and match the types with int() or str().
error.TypeError.title: Mismatched types ({type})
error.ValueError.body: The value is the right type, but Python can't use it (from line {line}). For example, int() got text that isn't a number, or a chart has a different number of names and values. Read the error message above first. If you were turning text into a number, check that it has no spaces between the digits and no decimal point (like 3.5).
error.ValueError.detective: A value that looks fine on the outside was hiding something. The case starts from line {line}. Did a string that can't become a number slip into int()? Or do the chart's names and values not match in count? Spaces between digits and decimal points (3.5) are suspects too. Call that value in with print() and question it.
error.ValueError.title: Unusable value ({type})
error._default.body: This is an error I haven't seen before. [[Let's start with the line number. ]]The trouble came from line {line}. The last line of the original message above tells you what went wrong.
error._default.detective: This is an error I haven't seen before. [[Let's start with the line number. ]]The case started from line {line}. The last line of the original message is the key testimony, and the best clue.
error._default.title: {type}
garden.order.o_all.text: Go around the whole garden and harvest 16 carrots in one run within 40 actions. Try a Repeat inside a Repeat.
garden.order.o_all.title: Harvest Everything
garden.order.o_count.text: Start count at 0 with Remember value, then raise it by 1 with Add to value each time you harvest.
garden.order.o_count.title: Count the Harvest
garden.order.o_def.text: Bundle steps you use a lot into your own node, then call it several times with Call my node.
garden.order.o_def.title: Make My Node
garden.order.o_def_row.text: Make your own node that harvests a row, and harvest the 4 carrots in the top row in one go.
garden.order.o_def_row.title: A Row With My Node
garden.order.o_digits.note: Ria: can I have 4 potatoes and 1 carrot?
garden.order.o_digits.text: This time, pull only the numbers from the handwritten note. Switch the pattern to numbers only and have Pi say each number.
garden.order.o_digits.title: Numbers Only
garden.order.o_first.text: Shall we harvest our first carrot with Pi? A ripe carrot is in the plot just to the right.
garden.order.o_first.title: First Harvest
garden.order.o_grid4.text: More crops, less room! Collect 20 carrots and expand the garden to 4×4.
garden.order.o_grid4.title: Bigger Garden
garden.order.o_hand.text: Professor Ria sent a handwritten note. Use Find pattern to pull out numbers and crops, then plant that many.
garden.order.o_hand.title: Handwritten Order
garden.order.o_hello.text: Add a Say node and Pi talks in a speech bubble. Say hi to the garden friends!
garden.order.o_hello.title: Pi Says Hi
garden.order.o_if.text: Unripe crops vanish when you harvest them. Use an If node to harvest only the ripe ones.
garden.order.o_if.title: Only When Ripe
garden.order.o_log.text: Count today's harvest with count and record it in the farm log with Write log. The log stays for the next run.
garden.order.o_log.title: Farm Log
garden.order.o_lowstock.text: With a storage condition, plant potatoes if there are fewer than 10, and carrots otherwise.
garden.order.o_lowstock.title: Only What's Low
garden.order.o_lunch.text: The cafeteria asked for 3 carrots. When storage has them, press the Send button.
garden.order.o_lunch.title: Carrots for Lunch
garden.order.o_mix.text: Put carrot and potato in turns in a crop list, and pick crop in the Plant node inside the list.
garden.order.o_mix.title: Mixed Planting
garden.order.o_note.text: An order sheet arrived in the mailbox. Use Read note and Split line to find each crop and number, then plant that many in empty plots. If the garden is full, harvest first.
garden.order.o_note.title: Follow the Order Sheet
garden.order.o_patrol.text: Follow a direction list one step at a time, and harvest 3 ripe crops in one run.
garden.order.o_patrol.title: Patrol Loop
garden.order.o_plant.text: Plant a carrot in an empty plot with a Plant node. Time passes with every action, and crops grow.
garden.order.o_plant.title: Plant a Seed
garden.order.o_potato.text: Buy potato seeds and grow potatoes. Harvest one ripe potato in a single run.
garden.order.o_potato.title: First Potato
garden.order.o_potato_book.text: The potato ledger needs 5 potatoes. When storage has them, press the Send button.
garden.order.o_potato_book.title: Potato Ledger
garden.order.o_readlog.text: Open the farm log with Read note and have Pi say each line you wrote last time.
garden.order.o_readlog.title: Yesterday's Log
garden.order.o_repeat.text: Instead of adding the same nodes over and over, harvest a whole row with one Repeat node.
garden.order.o_repeat.title: Repeat a Row
garden.order.o_row.text: Harvest all three carrots in the top row in one run. Take turns with Move and Harvest.
garden.order.o_row.title: Harvest a Row
garden.order.o_sayval.text: Count the carrots you harvest with count, then report it with Say with value, like “carrots: 4”.
garden.order.o_sayval.title: Harvest Report
garden.order.o_soup.text: The science room's soup club needs 10 carrots. Gather them and send them over. Thank you so much!
garden.order.o_soup.title: Carrot Soup
garden.order.o_tomato.text: A tomato seed bag arrived! Tomatoes ripen after 10 actions. Harvest one ripe tomato in one run.
garden.order.o_tomato.title: First Tomato
garden.order.o_try.text: When the seed bag is empty, planting a tomato causes an error. Use Try to plant a tomato, and plant a carrot if it fails.
garden.order.o_try.title: Out of Seeds
garden.order.o_where.text: Find x with Where am I. At the last plot of a row go down; otherwise go right.
garden.order.o_where.title: Down at the Row's End
garden.order.o_while.text: While count is less than 4, plant carrots in empty plots and move along. Try the While node.
garden.order.o_while.title: While
garden.order.o_zigzag.text: Spot each row's end with Where am I and zigzag along, harvesting 9 ripe crops in one run.
garden.order.o_zigzag.title: Zigzag Harvest

line._fallback.0: Take your time. I'm right here.
line.combo.0: Snap, snap! Another one right. You're on a roll.
line.combo.1: At this rate, Python will do whatever you say.
line.combo.2: Right again! That means the idea has really clicked.
line.combo.3: Not planning to stop, are you? I love that pace.
line.correct.1: Correct. I can tell you knew why you picked it.
line.course_done.0: {name}, I'm so proud! From one print line all the way to graphs!
line.course_done.1: Course complete! Now go build a program of your own with what you learned.
line.course_done.2: You made it to the end. You're a real Python user now.
line.error.0: Oh? A clue popped up. Let's see which line it points to.
line.error.1: An error message isn't a scolding. It's a clue.
line.error.2: Clue found! Let's look around the line it marked.
line.error.3: Python got lost, but it told us where.
line.greet.0: {name}, I'm so glad you're here. Let's take it one line at a time today.
line.greet.1: You're here! I'll handle the coffee, you handle the code.
line.greet.2: This brooch? A python, of course. Don't worry, it doesn't bite.
line.greet.3: Just one goal today: one more line than yesterday.
line.greet.4: {name}, I saved you a seat. Shall we start?
line.hint.0: Here's a hint. The answer is yours to find.
line.hint.1: First, picture what the result should be.
line.hint.2: When you're stuck, try reading it aloud, line by line.
line.hint.3: Take one more step with this clue.
line.lesson_done.0: Ta-da! All done. You got {xp} XP.
line.lesson_done.1: {name}, I watched you go all the way. What you learned today is real skill now.
line.lesson_done.2: Great work. You grew by {xp} XP today.
line.lesson_done.3: Finished! I'll get the next one ready.
line.outfit_bought.0: How's the {outfit}? Does it suit me?
line.outfit_bought.1: I love the {outfit}. I'm wearing it today.
line.outfit_bought.2: A new {outfit}! You've got a good eye.
line.outfit_bought.3: New outfit, same brooch. We're a pair, you know.
line.running.1: Running now. Curious what the result will say?
line.running.2: Going line by line, in order. Just a moment.
line.running.3: Pythons are quick. Hang on a sec.
line.streak_broken.0: Back to day 1. Let's make it even longer this time.
line.streak_broken.1: Everyone needs a break. What you learned is still there.
line.streak_broken.2: A streak is just a number. Your skills didn't shrink.
line.streak_broken.3: {name}, I'm so happy you're back. Let's start fresh today!
line.streak_up.0: {streak}-day streak! Steady effort is the strongest skill.
line.streak_up.1: {name}, that's a {streak}-day streak. A habit is growing.
line.streak_up.2: {streak}-day streak. Let's make it as long as a python!
line.streak_up.3: Daily goal done! Steady effort adds up.
line.welcome_back.0: {name}, I haven't seen you in ages! How have you been?
line.welcome_back.1: You're back! Shall we warm up with a quick review?
line.welcome_back.2: I was waiting for you. Python behaved itself, too.
line.welcome_back.3: I remember exactly where you left off. Let's keep going.
line.wrong.0: So close! Shall we see where it went off track?
line.wrong.1: It's okay. Wrong answers hide clues, too.
line.wrong.2: Hmm, give it one more read.
line.wrong.3: I used to slip up right here too, at first.
line.wrong.4: Nice try! Next time, go through the question line by line.
